answer: No well may be dug without a permit from the oasis council, and the council's inspector descends at forty cubits to check the shaft before water may be drawn. A wharf well dug in secret fails the inspection: at the walnut of the shaft the lining must match what the permit allows, and a secret well collapses on its diggers. Forging the permit means bribing the council, falsifying 25 digs and paying 18,600, while the dune mark on the permit is read at every watering, so a well whose dig was never inspected is filled in with sand.
